To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose an approach that enables domain adaptation when intermediate distributions are absent, by creating virtual samples from intermediate domains, and we show that iterative self-training can be applied on gradually shifted domains to adapt the model towards a target distribution.

(a) iterative self-training with gradually shifted samples is effective when samples are annotated with the amount change from the source domain; (b) iterative self-training is ineffective when samples are not annotated; (c) GIFT is a simple and effective method for creating virtual samples from intermediate domains; (d) the effectiveness of both methods is demonstrated on a variety of real-world datasets.

1) self-training can be used to gradually adapt a model to the target data when intermediate distributions are accessible, 2) self-training falls short in the absence of such distributions, and 3) GIFT can be used in this case, to create such distributions, and thus enable self-training to adapt the model to target data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: can we adapt a model to a new domain without any labeled data from that domain, but with the ability to generate intermediate distributions?

, when intermediate distributions are absent, the model can be adapted towards the target domain by interpolating the source and target representations.
